title: Priority-based export throttling and delivery quarantine for failed or late customer CSV exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Scheduled customer exports (CSV/S3 drop and webhook deliveries) have variable latency under load and a small set of noisy tenants can cause cascading retries, long delivery tails, and bursty queue buildup. We continue to see multi-hour retry storms that blow SLOs for other tenants and increase costs. Problem statement: implement a delivery-side mechanism that (1) prioritizes high-SLA/reserved-capacity tenants, (2) applies adaptive throttling and exponential backoff for noisy tenants, and (3) quarantines exports that repeatedly fail or exceed delivery latency thresholds for manual review and alternate delivery attempts. Goal: reduce cross-tenant impact from noisy exports, improve P95 delivery latency for standard exports, and provide clear tooling for support to inspect and re-run quarantined exports. Success criteria are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Priority queue implemented: exports tagged by tenant priority (reserved, paid, free) and routed accordingly.
Adaptive throttling: per-tenant token-bucket with dynamic rate limits based on recent failure rate and queue depth.
Quarantine area: failed exports moved to a quarantined S3 prefix and marked in console with reason and retry recommendations.
Delivery circuit-breaker: tenants that exceed N consecutive failures are automatically reduced in concurrency and moved to slow-path retries.
Observability: dashboards for delivery_latency_p50/p95, quarantined_exports_count, retry_storms_by_tenant, and a support view in Console.
Automated rerun: support can trigger idempotent re-run of quarantined exports from Console with audit trail and signed manifest.
Canary rollout: feature gated and rolled to 5% of tenants, then 25%, then 100% with rollback plan.
No regressions: existing successful delivery throughput for reserved capacity tenants remains within 5% of baseline during canary.
design_summary: We will introduce a delivery controller that sits between the export scheduler and the delivery workers. The controller maintains a priority-aware queue implemented on top of Redis streams (existing pattern in export dispatcher). Each tenant has metadata: priority_tier, recent_failure_count, last_success_timestamp, and token_bucket_rate. The controller enforces concurrency limits per-tenant and global caps, and adjusts token_bucket_rate by observing a sliding window failure ratio. When failure thresholds are crossed (configurable N failures or latency > X hours), the export is moved to a quarantined S3 prefix: s3://exports-quarantine/{tenant_id}/{export_id}/ with a failure manifest (reason, error payload, delivery attempts). Quarantined exports are surfaced in the Console support UI with actions: retry-immediate, retry-staggered, download, mark-as-manual. For webhook deliveries we add a delivery-signature header and preserve non-idempotent behavior by storing idempotency_token on export manifest. Concurrency reductions and slow-path retries use exponential backoff with jitter.
